from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Intuition: Transformations as Geometric Movement", 
                          ["Transformations map vectors to new vectors.", 
                           "Grid lines must remain parallel.", 
                           "The origin always stays fixed."])
        
        # Setup coordinate plane
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.5}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(plane)
        
        vector = Vector([1, 1], color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(vector, 'D3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(vector))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Shear transformation
        matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            vector.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Basis Vectors", [
            "Any 2D vector is a basis combination.",
            "Basis vectors are i-hat and j-hat.",
            "Transformations depend on basis vector movement."
        ])
        
        # Define base vectors
        i_hat = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color="#FF0000", buff=0)
        j_hat = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        i_label = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color="#FF0000").next_to(i_hat.get_end(), DOWN)
        j_label = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color="#00FF00").next_to(j_hat.get_end(), LEFT)
        basis_group = VGroup(i_hat, j_hat, i_label, j_label)
        
        self.place_at_grid(basis_group, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(basis_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Indicate(i_hat), Indicate(j_hat))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Rotate and scale to simulate transformation
        new_i = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5 + UP*0.5, color="#FF0000", buff=0)
        new_j = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=LEFT*0.5 + UP*1.2, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(i_hat, new_i),
            ReplacementTransform(j_hat, new_j),
            i_label.animate.next_to(new_i.get_end(), RIGHT),
            j_label.animate.next_to(new_j.get_end(), UP)
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Matrices are concise transformation containers.",
            "Columns store new basis positions.",
            "Matrix multiplication applies these changes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Matrix: Encoding the Transformation", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        matrix = Matrix([[1, -1], [2, 1]]).set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        i_hat_col = matrix.get_columns()[0].copy().set_color(RED)
        j_hat_col = matrix.get_columns()[1].copy().set_color(GREEN)
        
        # Highlight columns
        self.play(
            matrix.get_columns()[0].animate.set_color(RED),
            matrix.get_columns()[1].animate.set_color(GREEN)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(PURPLE)
        vec_v = Matrix([[3], [2]]).set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(vec_v, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        eq = MathTex("=").next_to(vec_v, RIGHT)
        result = Matrix([[1], [8]]).set_color(WHITE)
        result.next_to(eq, RIGHT)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(vec_v), Write(eq))
        self.play(FadeIn(result))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Application in Computer Graphics", [
            "Matrices perform complex geometric operations.",
            "Scaling and rotation are matrix multiplications.",
            "They power modern graphics engines."
        ])

        # Objects
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(square, 'B2', 'E5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(square))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(
            square.animate.scale(0.7),
            Rotate(square, angle=PI/4)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(
            Indicate(square, color=GREEN),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Linear Transformations and Matrices: The Geometry of Change

sections.title: Intuition: Transformations as Geometric Movement
sections.content: Define a linear transformation as a function that maps vectors to vectors, preserving grid lines (parallel remains parallel) and keeping the origin fixed.
sections.example: Imagine a digital 'Cat' character on a 2D plane. A transformation stretches, rotates, or shears the cat while ensuring its whiskers (vectors) remain connected to the origin.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Basis Vectors
sections.content: Explain that any 2D vector [x, y] is just a combination of basis vectors i-hat [1, 0] and j-hat [0, 1]. The transformation is defined entirely by where these two vectors land.
sections.example: Visualize a grid with two unit arrows. When we 'transform' the space, we track only where these two specific arrows point after the move.

sections.title: The Matrix: Encoding the Transformation
sections.content: Introduce the matrix as a concise container. The columns of the matrix represent the new coordinates of i-hat and j-hat. Matrix-vector multiplication is simply applying this change to any input vector.
sections.example: If i-hat moves to [1, 2] and j-hat moves to [-1, 1], the matrix is [[1, -1], [2, 1]]. Multiply this by a vector [3, 2] to see where the 'Cat''s foot lands.

sections.title: Synthesis: Application in Computer Graphics
sections.content: Summarize how matrices allow us to perform complex operations (rotations/scaling) by simple multiplication, forming the backbone of video game engines and animation.
sections.example: Show a 2D robot character spinning: each frame is just the robot's current position matrix multiplied by a 'rotation' matrix.
